introduction: The scriptures promise a 'meeting with God'. These readings say how that promise is kept: since the Essence cannot be met, to stand in the presence of the Manifestation is to attain the presence of God, and whoever turns to him has turned to God's face. On that ground Bahá’u’lláh grieves over those who waited for the day and missed it, tells those who came that they heard what Moses heard, assures those who could not come that the reward of meeting is written for them, and remembers by name those who did; later passages speak of that presence after death and of turning toward it in prayer. A hundred of the guide's hundred and eighty-two quotations are read here, ten from each tenth of the reading order, beside a hundred from elsewhere. Most stand alongside: 'he that hath seen me hath seen the Father', 'he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me', the Qur'an's 'the hand of God is above their hands', the bush, Job's 'now mine eye seeth thee', Simeon, the wise men and the queen of Sheba, 'blessed are they that have not seen'. Eight push back or add a side: Paul and Barnabas refusing divine honours, the Qur'an's 'vision comprehendeth him not' and its ban on any prophet saying 'be slaves of me', Hallaj, Whitman's letters from God in the street, Jesus's 'ye have done it unto me', God's countenance 'whithersoever ye turn', and Ezekiel beside the readings' 'woe'.
questions: Why, according to the readings, can the 'meeting with God' only mean meeting his Manifestation? What scriptural promise are they explaining?
'Whoso turneth unto Him hath turned unto God.' How is this like John's 'he that hath seen me hath seen the Father', and how do the readings keep it from the claim the Qur'an forbids?
Many who longed for the day are said to have missed it. What kept them back, and what would have helped?
Those who could not travel are promised the reward of presence. What does that say about what 'presence' is?
Matthew places the meeting in 'the least of these'; Whitman finds letters from God in the street. Do these widen the readings or contradict them?
What does it mean, now, to 'seek His presence'?

outside.why: A psalmist says: when thou saidst, seek ye my face, my heart said unto thee, thy face, Lord, will I seek.
Jesus told Thomas: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
Paul wrote to people he could not visit: though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit.
Jesus said: him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.
God tells Moses: thou canst not see my face, for there shall no man see me, and live.
John's Gospel says that no man hath seen God at any time; the Son hath declared him.
When Philip asked to be shown the Father, Jesus answered: he that hath seen me hath seen the Father.
John says that he came unto his own, and his own received him not.
The Qur'an says: whoever hopeth for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work.
A psalmist says that a day in God's courts is better than a thousand elsewhere.

At Lystra a crowd cried that the gods had come down in the likeness of men, and Paul and Barnabas rent their clothes in refusal. What separates the readings' claim from the one those apostles refused?
The Qur'an says: vision comprehendeth him not. How do the readings hold this together with the promise of 'meeting God'?
Job says: though worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God.
Jesus told those he sent: he that despiseth you despiseth me, and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.
The Qur'an says that those who swear allegiance to the Prophet swear allegiance only to God; the hand of God is above their hands.
Jesus said: I have not spoken of myself; the Father which sent me gave me a commandment what I should speak.
Jesus cried: he that believeth on me believeth on him that sent me, and he that seeth me seeth him that sent me.
Jesus told his messengers: he that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
Paul speaks of the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

The Qur'an says no one given the Scripture and prophethood could say to people 'be slaves of me instead of God'. How do the readings keep 'whoso turneth unto Him hath turned unto God' on the right side of that verse?
Paul says of Christ that all things were created by him, and for him.
Jesus wept over Jerusalem: if thou hadst known, in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace.
Jesus lamented over the city that kills the prophets: how often would I have gathered thy children, and ye would not.
His own townspeople said of Jesus: is not this the carpenter? And they were offended at him.
Paul observes that not many wise, not many mighty, not many noble were called.
Ezekiel hears God say: I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn and live. How should the 'woe' of this reading be heard beside that?
Jesus told his disciples that many prophets desired to see the things they saw, and did not see them.
John's Gospel says this is the condemnation: light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light.
Jesus said of his hearers that seeing they see not, and hearing they hear not.
The Pharisees asked: have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him?
These are the words Moses heard in the Qur'an: lo, I, even I, am God; there is no God save me.
In Exodus God calls to Moses from the midst of the bush: put off thy shoes, for the place is holy ground.
Israel said at Horeb: we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire, and have seen that God doth talk with man.
The Apocalypse ends with a promise: his servants shall serve him, and they shall see his face.
Simeon, holding the child in the temple, said: mine eyes have seen thy salvation.
Whitman said: I find letters from God dropt in the street, and every one is signed by God's name. Does the divine breeze pass by on certain days only?
The angel of the nativity said: I bring you good tidings of great joy; unto you is born this day a Saviour.
Isaiah says that the excellency of Carmel and Sharon shall see the glory of the Lord.
The Song of Songs has the beloved say: I am come into my garden.
Isaiah's servant is despised and rejected of men, and we esteemed him not.
Paul tells the Colossians to set their affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
Jesus said: ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find.
A psalmist desires one thing: to dwell in the house of the Lord, and to behold his beauty.
A psalmist says: the law of thy mouth is better unto me than thousands of gold and silver.
Paul counted all things but loss for the excellency of knowing Christ.
When the star appeared, wise men came from the east asking where the child was.
Esther knew that no one enters the king's inner court uncalled, unless he hold out the golden sceptre.
Paul wrote to friends he had not met: I long to see you, that I may be comforted together with you.
Paul asked a church: what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even ye?
The elder writes: I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full.
Peter writes to those who never saw Jesus: whom having not seen, ye love, and rejoice with joy unspeakable.
David, who could not build the temple, was told: thou didst well that it was in thine heart.
Paul says that where there is first a willing mind, it is accepted according to what a man hath.
A saying of Muhammad holds that every person will have the reward of what he intended.
John's first letter speaks for those who were there: that which we have seen with our eyes and our hands have handled.
Hebrews says: let us come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy.
Jesus told his disciples to rejoice because their names are written in heaven.
Malachi says a book of remembrance was written before the Lord for them that thought upon his name.
When the wise men saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
Paul blesses a friend who sought him out in his imprisonment and was not ashamed of his chain.
Hebrews says that Abraham, when he was called, obeyed and went out, not knowing whither he went.
Boaz praises Ruth for leaving her father, her mother and the land of her nativity, and asks a full reward for her.
Certain Greeks at the feast came to a disciple and said: Sir, we would see Jesus.
A psalmist asks: what shall I render unto the Lord for all his benefits toward me?
Isaiah calls: ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters.
The queen of Sheba said on arriving: I believed not the words until I came; the half was not told me.
An Ethiopian official travelled to Jerusalem to worship, and was reading the prophet Isaiah on the way home.
A psalm blesses those in whose heart are the ways, who go from strength to strength till each appears before God.
Zacchaeus sought to see Jesus who he was, and climbed a tree to do it.
The council looked at two unlearned men and took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
Jesus said: blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
The priestly blessing asks that the Lord make his face shine upon thee, and lift up his countenance upon thee.
Job says at the end: I had heard of thee by the hearing of the ear, but now mine eye seeth thee.
Peter said: Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.
In Matthew's judgment scene the King says: inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Where else is the presence met?
Paul says that we all, beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image.
Hebrews calls the Son the brightness of God's glory and the express image of his person.
Hallaj said: I am he whom I love, and he whom I love is I; if thou seest me, thou seest him. How do the readings tell the mirror from a claim of identity?
A psalmist says: I will behold thy face in righteousness; I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.
A psalm asks, as the hart pants for water: when shall I come and appear before God?
Mark says of the crowds around Jesus, in one line, that the common people heard him gladly.
Paul thanks God for a faith that dwelt first in Timothy's grandmother and mother.
Mordecai asked Esther: who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
Proverbs says that children's children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children are their fathers.
Proverbs says of a good mother that her children arise up and call her blessed.
Paul wrote to the bereaved that they should not sorrow as others which have no hope.
The Qur'an says to the soul at peace: return unto thy Lord, content in his good pleasure.
Paul says: for to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
Tennyson hoped to see his Pilot face to face when he had crossed the bar.
Paul says: now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.
A psalm of pilgrimage says: I was glad when they said unto me, let us go into the house of the Lord.
Daniel prayed three times a day with his windows open toward Jerusalem.
The Qur'an fixes a direction for prayer: turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship.
Solomon asked that God hear the prayers his people make toward the house he had built.
The Qur'an also says that the East and the West are God's: whithersoever ye turn, there is God's countenance. What does a point of adoration add to that?
Jesus said: seek ye first the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added unto you.
John's first letter says that when he shall appear we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is.
A psalm says: my soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of the Lord.
A dying man asked Jesus: Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
A psalmist asks: whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.

revelation-they-shall-see-his-face.text: And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads

psalm-thy-face-will-i-seek.text: When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, Thy face, Lord, will I seek

psalm-satisfied-with-thy-likeness.text: As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness

psalm-better-than-thousands-of-gold.text: The law of thy mouth is better unto me than thousands of gold and silver

kings-pray-toward-this-place.text: That thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which thou hast said, My name shall be there: that thou mayest hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall make toward this place. And hearken thou to the supplication of thy servant, and of thy people Israel, when they shall pray toward this place: and hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place: and when thou hearest, forgive

quran-turn-thy-face-toward.text: We have seen the turning of thy face to heaven (for guidance, O Muhammad). And now verily We shall make thee turn (in prayer) toward a qiblah which is dear to thee. So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship, and ye (O Muslims), wheresoever ye may be, turn your faces (when ye pray) toward it. Lo! Those who have received the Scripture know that (this revelation) is the Truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.

john-epistle-which-we-have-seen.text: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life; (For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us;) That which we have seen and heard declare we unto you
